title: Reactive runbook fibers: lightweight admin choreographer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight choreography layer ("runbook fibers") that composes small, event-driven admin primitives into safe, observable repair and maintenance flows. Fibers are single-purpose fragments (eg. rotate-credentials, restart-worker, refresh-cache) that can be wired reactively based on triggers (alerts, schedules, console actions). The choreographer routes events, enforces RBAC and dry-run semantics, records immutable audit trails, and provides a minimal replay/dryrun mode for oncall. Goal is to convert a subset of existing bulky runbooks into composable fibers that reduce operator time-to-remediate and make automated shortpatches safer and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Define fiber manifest schema and validation (inputs, idempotency contract, required secrets) and publish on Confluence
Choreographer accepts an event and executes a 2-step fiber sequence with RBAC gate, producing structured telemetry and an audit entry
Dry-run mode returns simulated actions and diffable output without changing infra or secrets
Canary: enable fibers for a single service team with feature-flagging and rollback path
End-to-end test harness that replays synthetic failure events and validates observability (logs, traces, metrics)
implementation_steps: Design fiber manifest and idempotency contract; iterate with SRE/Oncall
Implement choreographer API: submit-event, dryrun, status, replay
Build minimal runner that executes fibers in sandboxed env (k8s Job with restricted service account)
Add audit export to internal event-store and wire to Console event timeline
Create e2e test harness and synthetic incidents for validation
Run canary with one team, collect metrics (MTTR, false-positive runs, cost), refine safety gates
notes: Trade-offs: synchronous orchestration gives simpler semantics but increases oncall latency; chose evented choreography with optional sync wait-for-completion for critical flows
Security: fibers must declare secret scopes; runner uses short-lived tokens issued from KMS/HSM-backed broker
Reusability: aim for <20 lines per fiber; encourage composing existing shelllets into typed adapters
Observability: emit structured JSON events with standard keys (actor, fiber_id, inputs_hash, result_code) to trace across services
